name: LAN-Games
description: Self-hosted LAN board game platform: eight turn-based classics — Monopoly, Risk, Battleship, Yahtzee, Life, Checkers, Connect Four, and Tic-Tac-Toe — playable in any browser on your network. Real-time multiplayer via Socket.IO, with lobbies, hidden-information support (Battleship/Risk), and spectator mode. Unlike most party game servers it has real user accounts: JWT-based auth with bcrypt-hashed passwords, and game state persists in a SQLite database (mount the data path so it survives updates). Designed for trusted local networks — don't expose it to the internet. Turnkey setup: the login-token secret (JWT) is auto-generated on first boot and persisted in the data directory; optionally override it under advanced settings.

paths.name: Game Data
paths.description: SQLite database directory — user accounts and game state live here. Ownership is fixed automatically on startup (set to PUID:PGID), then the app runs unprivileged.

ports.name: WebUI Port
ports.description: Host port for the LAN Games web UI.

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: User ID the app runs as after startup (Unraid default: 99 = nobody). Data files are owned by this user.

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: Group ID the app runs as after startup (Unraid default: 100 = users).

variables.name: JWT Secret (optional)
variables.description: Secret used to sign login tokens. Leave EMPTY for turnkey setup: the container generates one on first boot and persists it in the Game Data directory (.jwt_secret), so logins survive restarts and updates. Set a value only to override with your own secret.
